newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields track Germany lower.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields track Germany lower.

text.p: 1515 GMT - Swedish long debt yields closed lower on Tuesday, helped by record low German yields.
In the last hour of trade the market also saw large buying interest for Swedish bonds, dealers said.
"There have been some large buyers of Swedish bonds in the last hour of the session. It seems people have decided it's worth buying Swedish risk again," one head dealer said.

Six-month T-bill rates were unchanged at 4.03 percent while nine-year bond yields dropped five basis points to 6.64 percent. Meanwhile the crown firmed to 4.4280 against the mark compared to 4.4395 late on Monday.
"The fact that the crown has stopped falling together with last week's wage agreement by paper workers might have lent support to the debt market," one analyst said.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields decreased two basis points to 105.

In the afternoon Prime Minister Goran Persson said that Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom could be correct in his assessment that the European monetary union (EMU) does not risk developing into a federation.
This was also received positively, dealers said.
